summary: Ottoman-born Greek con man Basil Zaharoff became the leading salesman for Nordenfelt, Maxim and Vickers, stoking arms races and bribing officials across Europe in the decades before and during World War One.

evidence.note: birth in Anatolia (Mugla) to Greek parents posing as Russians; year from general knowledge
bigamous marriage in England, embezzlement trial and extradition from Belgium
years of scams and a second bigamous marriage in the United States
Nordenfelt had first hired him as a salesman in 1877; rejoins in the mid-1880s
submarine sales to Greece, Turkey and Russia that spark an arms race
French loans fund Russian rearmament won by Vickers; Paris newspapers used as propaganda
Snowden's 1914 Commons speech on arms firms owning officials; bribery in Russia
Briey iron basin left unshelled during the war through his influence
role in the 1920-22 Greco-Turkish war, then decline at Vickers and death in 1936

notes: main_span runs from his first Nordenfelt job (1877) to the Greco-Turkish war (1922), the end of his influence; his decline and death to 1936 are in covered_span. Setting puts France first as the main WWI theatre he profited from; Russia is where his biggest sales and their debt consequences played out. Vickers also stands in for the Maxim and Nordenfelt firms.
